newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Wall St seen shepherding S.Africa stocks next week.
newsitem.headline: Wall St seen shepherding S.Africa stocks next week.

text.p: South African stocks will next week look to Wall Street for guidance as interest in the local market will be held back by quiet Easter holiday trade, equity and porfolio managers said.
"We're into holiday season and there are a lot of portfolio managers away," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak told Reuters on Thursday.
"This market is jittery because of what's happening in the U.S. We'll watch the Dow closely," said Denzil Newman, Syfrets Managed Assets portfolio manager.

The Federal Reserve's 25 basis point hike in U.S. interest rates late Tuesday, although largely discounted by world markets earlier, is seen having some further impact on Wall Street and U.S. long bonds which would follow through into South Africa.
"The rate cut was discounted and figures out of the U.S. still indicate good growth in that economy. We'll still track Wall Street," Scott said.
Commentators here added that the local stock market undertone is firm and, providing there is no shake-up in U.S. shares, South African stocks will weather any hangover.

"Sentiment about our market is improving. Foreigners are showing reasonable interest in industrial and financial stocks this will underpin our market for a while. Local sentiment has also improved," Newman said.
With markets closed on Friday and Monday for the Easter holidays trade next week is seen dull.
"We see quite a flat market. The outlook is not terribly exciting," Scott said.
He added much of the expected flatness would continue for a while with the second quarter of the year traditionally flat.

Economic forecasts for South Africa were positive, recently announced company earnings were adding a glow and consumer confidence was starting to pick up boosting retail shares, equity and portfolio managers said.
"Earnings and economic forecasts are looking good and the retail sector is looking up after not looking so good for a while," Newman said.
But commentators said gold stocks would continue to be disappointing with the bullion price stuck around $350 an ounce and regularly stumbling below.

They added that one of the scarce positive factors likely to cheer gold was the announcement on Thursday that the Indonesian government had put the Busang gold find on hold after news the deposit might be nowhere near as large as had been reported.
Local economic indicators likely to offer markets direction next week are February's money supply and gold and foreign exchange reserves due on Wednesday.
There are no major company results expected.
